feature: Changing a clip's speed keeps the edit joined up
summary: Speeding a clip up no longer leaves black where it used to be, and slowing it down no longer runs over the next clip: the clips after it on its track move to meet it, and the transition on the next cut stays.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Measured with Scripts/playtest/speeding-up-a-clip-keeps-the-edit-joined-walk.json on the probe, plus SpeedRippleTests in PhotonzCore.

try.do: Open a recording and drag a second one onto V1 right after it so the two meet.
Click the cut between them and pick Cross dissolve in Transitions.
Click the first clip and choose Clip > Speed > 2x.
Play across the cut: no black, and the dissolve plays.
Press Command Z once: both clips go back where they were.
Choose Clip > Speed > 0.5x: the second clip is pushed along, not covered.

evaluate: Does the clip after the sped one land where you expect it, with no black in between?
Is it right that titles and music on other tracks stay where you put them while the picture track moves?
Does one Command Z feel like the right size of undo for a speed change?
rough: Chose rippling the clip's own track (and captions heard off it) over every track, matching Final Cut's primary storyline and Premiere's Speed with Ripple Edit, and a freeze's 'This track' default. A title or callout on another track over a later clip stays put, so it can end up over a different shot; Final Cut would carry a connected clip along, Photonz has no connected clips yet.
Speed stops on a ramp (Add Speed Stop, dragging a stop) still change a clip's length without moving the clips after it; this task covered constant speed only (Clip > Speed and set_speed).
No mock covers this: it is an edit rule, not a surface. Nothing on screen changed apart from where the clips land.
